chief_complaint: Acute bronchitis presenting with cough and respiratory symptoms (onset 2025-08-24)
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 42-year-old male who presented to the emergency department on 2025-08-24 with acute bronchitis. He reports recent cough and mild dyspnea. His chronic conditions include essential hypertension that remains in the stage‑2 range (139/97 mmHg) despite hydrochlorothiazide therapy, obesity (BMI ≥30), pre‑diabetes (A1c 6.2%), and anemia of unclear etiology. He has a long‑standing history of stress, social isolation, and intimate‑partner abuse, and is currently employed part‑time with a criminal record, all contributing to psychosocial strain. He uses inhaled fluticasone and albuterol, suggesting ongoing asthma that is not documented as an active problem. Overall, his clinical trajectory shows uncontrolled cardiometabolic risk factors, a recent respiratory infection, and significant social determinants affecting health maintenance.
